title: Hardwiring preserves polynomial size
statement: Let $a : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and for each input length $n$ let $D_n$ be a Boolean circuit on $n+a(n)$ input bits. For each $n$, fix an assignment $\alpha_n$ to the final $a(n)$ input bits. Suppose every $D_n$ is well-formed with fan-in at most two, and there are natural numbers $c,k$ such that the size of $D_n$ is at most $c(n+1)^k$ for every $n$. Then the language of strings $w$ accepted by $D_{|w|}$ when given $w$ followed by the fixed assignment $\alpha_{|w|}$ has polynomial circuit size with fan-in at most two.
